In the near term, the key swing factor is how effectively Mizuho executes on cost control and integration of businesses such as Rakuten Securities and Greenhill without eroding net margins. data.title: What Is Netflix (NFLX) Asking Regulators Through Its New Streaming Alliance?
data.description:

The coalition leans into the existing Narrative that advertising, live events and global franchises can support long term upside. The clearest test will come with upcoming US regulatory steps around the Sports Broadcasting Act review and any new rules on streaming sports exclusivity. That means that an insider was happy to buy shares at above the current price of AU$0.085. While their view may have changed since the purchase was made, this does at least suggest they have had confidence in the company's future. To us, it's very important to consider the price insiders pay for shares. Generally speaking, it catches our eye when an insider has purchased shares at above current prices, as it suggests they believed the shares were worth buying, even at a higher price. The only individual insider to buy over the last year was Alexius Chan.

Insider Ownership Of Vital Metals

Looking at the total insider shareholdings in a company can help to inform your view of whether they are well aligned with common shareholders. I reckon it's a good sign if insiders own a significant number of shares in the company. From our data, it seems that Vital Metals insiders own 10% of the company, worth about AU$2.2m. We do note, however, it is possible insiders have an indirect interest through a private company or other corporate structure. We do generally prefer see higher levels of insider ownership.

So What Does This Data Suggest About Vital Metals Insiders?

There haven't been any insider transactions in the last three months -- that doesn't mean much. However, our analysis of transactions over the last year is heartening. data.title: What Is Drawing Fresh Attention To Elastic (ESTC)?
data.description:

Elastic shares have pulled back recently, with a 7-day share price return down 9.17% and a 30-day share price return down 3.80%, even after a strong 90-day share price return of 38.73% that hints at earlier momentum now cooling. That mixed track record frames today’s product news and the current US$83.39 share price as part of a longer rebuilding phase after a 5-year total shareholder return that is down 47.99%.

data.title: Nasdaq (NDAQ) Expands Partnership To Build Tokenized Equity Infrastructure
data.description:
• Nasdaq (NasdaqGS:NDAQ) expanded its partnership with Payward, the operator of Kraken, to build tokenized equity trading infrastructure.
  • The collaboration includes developing Nasdaq Equity Tokens, or NETs, with an anticipated launch timeline in 2027.
  • The partners plan to roll out new market surveillance technology designed to monitor both traditional securities and digital asset trading.
  • The Nasdaq Equity Tokens and surveillance build out is only one part of what could shape Nasdaq's wider future direction. Take a look at 2 warning signs we have identified for Nasdaq.

Other exchanges, brokers, and technology vendors are also pushing into tokenized market plumbing and digital trading, so it is worth comparing them through 60 AI infrastructure stocks.

Nasdaq runs trading venues and market technology for capital markets in the US and overseas, so building tokenized equity and surveillance tools with Kraken fits directly into its role as a core infrastructure provider for exchanges and brokers.

4 things going right for Nasdaq that this headline doesn't cover.

How the Kraken Partnership Leans Into Nasdaq’s Tokenization Story

For Nasdaq, the expanded Kraken relationship plugs directly into its broader push to treat AI, cloud and tokenization as long-term platforms rather than side projects. The Narrative on Nasdaq is essentially a bet that these infrastructure bets can turn a traditional exchange group into a higher value technology provider.

"The enhanced partnership with AWS is expected to modernize Nasdaq's market infrastructure across its financial services clientele, driving operational efficiencies, improving scalability, and potentially increasing market share..."

See how the full story points towards a $110 fair value for Nasdaq.

The Kraken deal presses on the same lever as Nasdaq’s AWS work by shifting more of its equity market plumbing into always-on, programmable infrastructure. Investors focused only on crypto exposure may miss that NETs and xStocks are framed as issuer-centric, with governance and regulatory compliance built in, which lines up with the existing AI and cloud story rather than sitting outside it.

On the other hand, this partnership also leans into the Narrative’s key risk that Nasdaq relies heavily on big collaborations and complex integrations. Incumbents such as ICE and CME are also working on digital asset and surveillance offerings, so any delay in rolling out global trading, post-trade and surveillance for NETs would feed directly into those existing concerns about competitive pressure and execution.

The takeaway is simple: the same Kraken news can look like either welcome proof of Nasdaq’s tokenization thesis or an added layer of partnership risk, depending on which Narrative you already believe.

data.title: MP Materials (MP) Stock Looks Above Fair Value On Its 142% Run
data.description:
MP Materials has seen its share price move sharply in recent years, which puts a spotlight on whether the current US$50.51 quote is adequately grounded in the sales the business is generating. With rare earths policy and geopolitics in the headlines again, an open question is how much of MP Materials' valuation is tied to its actual revenue base rather than shifting sentiment.

  • Over the past 3 years, MP Materials has delivered a share price gain of 142.5%, which raises the stakes on whether the current valuation can still be reconciled with its sales.
  • Federal support for critical minerals projects and MP Materials' role as a beneficiary can shape expectations for future rare earths demand, which may support higher planned investment and influence how investors think about the level of sales needed to back today's stock price.
  • The analysts covering MP Materials have run their own numbers. See what analysts think MP Materials's shares could be worth.

The issue now is whether MP Materials' current share price is justified by the sales it is generating when judged against the Fair Ratio benchmark for this lens.

To see how MP Materials compares with other rare earth and critical minerals plays, line it up next to the 27 best rare earth metal stocks.

Does MP Materials Look Pricey on Sales?

P/S fits MP Materials because revenue is still the cleanest anchor while earnings and free cash flow remain volatile. On this yardstick, the stock trades on a P/S of 21.6x, which is far above the broader Metals and Mining industry average of 3.2x and well ahead of the 3.6x peer group level given here for rare earth and critical minerals players.

The Fair Ratio model, which adjusts the target multiple for MP Materials' growth profile, margins, scale and risk, flags the current 21.6x as overvalued and shows the figure well above what would usually be expected. Because the model is heavily penalising recent losses and cash burn, that gap is better read as a warning that the shares screen very expensive on this framework rather than a precise fair-value estimate. Despite federal backing and sector attention supporting sentiment, the valuation still assumes a lot of future revenue delivery already. Explore the numbers behind MP Materials's P/S valuation.
